channel.title: Latest alerts from washingtonpost.com
channel.description: An unofficial feed created by Derek Willis.

item.title: Columnist Monica Hesse has found the most perimenopausal show on television
item.description: In the fourth season of the Julian Fellowes period drama “The Gilded Age,” women of a certain age aren’t fretting over hot flashes. Instead, these middle-aged baddies are scheming and wielding social power.

item.title: Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis planning another White House run
item.description: Florida’s status as one of the few red states to mostly withstand the Democratic midterm sweep will be a core part of his argument, an adviser said.

item.title: Republicans took them for granted. Democrats wrote them off. No more.
item.description: What the midterms proved about the ‘God gap.’

item.title: Cornell faculty senate votes no confidence in university leadership
item.description: The symbolic vote comes in the aftermath of sexual assault allegations made by a former student.

item.title: Trump names Stephen Miller as new White House chief of staff
item.description: President Donald Trump's current White House chief of staff, Susie Wiles, is leaving her post.

item.title: You may be able to fire your internet provider for a cheaper, better option
item.description: Americans usually rely on cable or fiber for their at-home internet. But there's a third option that many may find attractive.

item.title: I removed my fallopian tubes. What if my stepmom asks for grandkids? Our Say More writers are giving advice.
item.description: Maura Judkis and Amy Parlapiano are answering reader questions.

item.title: Two top Justice Department officials resign, including the head of the national security division
item.description: John Eisenberg resigned, along with Jason Reding Quiñones, the head of the U.S. attorney’s office in Miami. That office is leading a conspiracy investigation into several of President Donald Trump’s foes. The two officials are the latest high-profile departures from the administration since the midterm elections.

item.title: Corporate America courted Trump. Now a blitz of Democratic investigations is coming.
item.description: Democrats are preparing for congressional inquiries into some of the country’s largest companies, according to people familiar with the plan, setting off a scramble among executives with close ties to President Donald Trump and his administration.

item.title: President JD Vance? More slogging through a sewer of odious politics.
item.description: Temperate Americans of all political stripes should unite to stymie the vice president’s ambitions.

item.title: U.S. economy added 165,000 jobs in October, showing surprising strength
item.description: The unemployment rate ticked down to 4.1 percent, near the same low levels over the past year, according to a Labor Department report.

item.title: Jay Rockefeller, who served as West Virginia governor and a five-term U.S. senator, dies at 89
item.description: John D. “Jay” Rockefeller IV, an heir to a vast oil fortune and a liberal Democrat who became a leading voice on health care and national security died Friday at his home in Washington, D.C. His family did not provide a cause.

item.title: Pete Hegseth. Senate races. Trump’s arch. Tumbling stocks. Death row. Heart risks. Calorific coffee. Catch up now.
item.description: Today’s seven most important and interesting stories.

item.title: Judge halts construction on Trump’s planned arch shortly after a federal panel approved it to proceed
item.description: U.S. District Judge Tanya S. Chutkan blocked the project, siding with military veterans and local government officials who had urged her to stop it. Opponents of the proposed arch say it is illegal and needs to be approved by the current Congress.

item.title: Federal panel led by Trump allies approves 250-foot arch, clearing the way for construction as a judge weighs whether to halt it
item.description: The National Capital Planning Commission gave final authorization for the memorial after more than eight hours of public testimony and heated debate. Over 120 people, including architects, historians and military veterans, urged administration officials not to proceed, saying the project would wrongly overshadow nearby Arlington National Cemetery and irrevocably change the Washington landscape.

item.title: New estrogen research may change how scientists think about women’s aging brains
item.description: Scientists are assessing the potential benefits of hormone therapy for older women’s cognition.

item.title: National Guard adding boats, Humvees in D.C. amid a new push by local officials to oust troops
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth authorized the fleet upgrades through the end of the year, according to an internal memo from Oct. 29 obtained Thursday by The Washington Post. The plans were revealed on the same day the D.C. Council’s public safety committee chair, Brooke Pinto (D-Ward 2), said she planned to ask incoming Democratic governors to end Guard deployments to Washington.

item.title: Here are the four looming constitutional showdowns
item.description: Here are the four looming constitutional showdowns

item.title: Opponents of Trump’s D.C. golf course overhaul ask judge to stop president from closing site
item.description: The National Park Service has said East Potomac Park needs to close Nov. 15 because it is unsafe, but preservationists say the president just wants to start work on a new course.

item.title: Republicans lose four more House seats in North Carolina upsets as GOP wipeout spreads
item.description: Democrats pulled off the wins Thursday in districts that President Donald Trump carried in 2024, following additional gains earlier. Other Republicans are still facing defeat in a state that is handing the GOP some of its biggest losses this cycle.

item.title: Karen Bass concedes to challenger Nithya Raman in Los Angeles mayoral race
item.description: Raman, the first Democratic Socialists of America-backed candidate elected to the Los Angeles City Council, tapped into frustration with Bass’s handling of wildfires, homelessness and cost of living.

item.title: Gov. Gavin Newsom moves to spare lives of all 548 prisoners on California's death row
item.description: The outgoing governor and potential 2028 presidential candidate said he has started the process to change the sentences to life in prison without the possibility of parole. If successful, the commutation would empty the nation’s largest death row.

item.title: Stocks tumble, erasing post-midterm gains as analysts weigh future of AI build-out
item.description: The S&P 500 had lost 4 percent by noon, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq composite index was down more than 5 percent. The drop comes amid fears the election results will slow the country’s construction of data centers.

item.title: Trump loyalist Harmeet Dhillon resigns as head of Justice Department’s civil rights division
item.description: The conservative attorney’s departure marks the first shake-up in the Justice Department since Democrats swept the midterm elections. During her time running the civil rights division, Dhillon oversaw the departure of hundreds of career staffers.

item.title: GOP’s midterm losses likely to raise pressure on older Supreme Court Justices Alito and Thomas to retire soon
item.description: The lame-duck session will probably be President Donald Trump’s last chance to get a high court nominee confirmed by the Senate if either Justices Samuel A. Alito Jr., 76, or Clarence Thomas, 78, chooses to step down. In early January, the Democratic Party takes control of both houses of Congress.

item.title: ‘Knives out’ at Pentagon: After unpopular Iran war dooms GOP in midterms, Hegseth is vulnerable, officials say
item.description: Although President Donald Trump has continued to support Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, questions have arisen about whether Trump will hold someone at the Pentagon accountable for Republicans’ big electoral losses.

item.title: JD Vance is test-driving a delusional new message
item.description: Trumpism Lite in 2028? Good luck, JD and Marco.

item.title: GOP blame game. Democrats’ plans. Trump ballroom. Supreme Court. Frats. Aging brains. Healthier bread. Catch up now.
item.description: Today’s seven most important and interesting stories.

item.title: How Republican missteps laid the groundwork for a historic midterm rebuke
item.description: Republicans began the midterm election season with a favorable Senate map, aggressive plans to redraw House districts and access to enormous sums of money. But the president underestimated how angry voters had grown at his handling of the economy, tariffs and the war he launched in Iran this year, alienating key segments of the coalition he built in his historic 2024 win.

item.title: Stocks surged and oil prices fell as markets responded to the midterm rout
item.description: Voters in many states favored limits on AI, a key driver of the economy. But a split between Congress and the White House may signal something else to investors.

item.title: ‘A lot of finger-pointing’: Texas is in shock
item.description: ‘A lot of finger-pointing’: Texas is in shock

item.title: Trump concedes that Iran war angered voters and triggered Democratic landslide
item.description: After Vice President JD Vance and others in the GOP blamed the war for Tuesday’s rout, President Donald Trump agreed — but said he would do it again.

item.title: Voters rightly punished Trumpism. But please hold the giddiness, George F. Will writes.
item.description: Voters rightly punished Trumpism. But please hold the giddiness, George F. Will writes.

item.title: Democratic women surge past 100 House seats as Republican women lose ground
item.description: Voters also elected the country’s first Black and first Native American female governors as women won a record number of governorships.

item.title: Now it’s clear who could save the Democratic brand
item.description: Centrists won almost every one of the most competitive midterms battles.

item.title: Vance breaks sharply with Trump, blaming Republicans’ midterm losses on administration’s handling of Iran war
item.description: While Trump and his top White House advisers blamed Republican candidates and tried to wash their hands of any responsibility for the GOP’s massive losses, Vice President JD Vance, a potential 2028 contender, pinned the blame on the Trump administration’s decisions.

item.title: Mike Johnson (R-Louisiana) won’t seek House minority leader position after midterm losses
item.description: Ahead of the elections, two other House GOP leaders — Majority Leader Steve Scalise (Louisiana) and Judiciary Committee Chair Jim Jordan (Ohio) — signaled plans to run for minority leader regardless of Johnson’s intentions.

item.title: Former federal prosecutor appointed by N.Y. attorney general to lead investigation into alleged gang rape at Cornell University
item.description: New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the appointment of Jacqueline Kelly as outside counsel on Wednesday.

item.title: Double-digit swings in rural areas, suburbs and major cities fueled Democrats’ midterm wins. See the groups that shifted the most.
item.description: The results included new high-water marks for Democrats, whose victories in several states were their first in decades.

item.title: A historic blue wave overtakes Congress as Trump distances himself from GOP losses. Follow our live coverage and analysis.
item.description: Democrats claimed both the House and Senate as Republicans suffered their biggest defeat in half a century. Two Senate races — in Alaska and Mississippi — and more than 60 House races remain uncalled.

item.title: Blue wave. Key results. Demographic shifts. Trump blame. Reflecting Pool. ADHD. Legend of Zelda. Catch up now.
item.description: Today’s seven most important and interesting stories.

item.title: Michigan elects Abdul El-Sayed as nation’s first Muslim senator, AP reports, giving Democrats at least 54 votes in chamber
item.description: El-Sayed defeated former congressman Mike Rogers (R) in one of the most closely watched and hard-fought contests of the midterms. He will succeed Sen. Gary Peters (D), who is retiring.

item.title: Democrats take control of House and Senate as voters deal Trump a historic repudiation in midterms
item.description: Democrats won in places they hadn’t carried in decades amid voter discontent over high prices and the war in Iran. Republicans also suffered from a collapse in turnout, as fewer of their supporters showed up on Election Day than four years ago, according to preliminary turnout data.

item.title: Sen. Susan Collins (R) of Maine loses reelection bid to Troy Jackson (D), according to AP
item.description: Collins, who was seeking a sixth term, had distanced herself from President Donald Trump while campaigning in the blue state. Jackson, the former president of the state Senate, became Democrats’ pick after Graham Platner withdrew.

item.title: How Trump and Democrats can navigate divided government
item.description: How Trump and Democrats can navigate divided government

item.title: Democrats made the midterms about Trump. Voters responded, David Ignatius writes.
item.description: Democrats made the midterms about Trump. Voters responded, David Ignatius writes.

item.title: Democrats win control of Senate, as Josh Turek flips seat in Iowa, according to AP
item.description: Democrats have now seized GOP seats in Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, North Carolina, South Carolina and Texas, giving them the majority in the Senate. Turek, a member of the state legislature, targeted President Donald Trump’s tariffs and high gas prices driven by the Iran war. He will succeed Sen. Joni Ernst (R), who is retiring.

item.title: Kansas picks a Democrat for Senate for the first time in nearly a century, ousting incumbent Roger Marshall (R), AP reports
item.description: The first-term senator lost to Adam Hamilton (D), the founding pastor of a megachurch who received endorsements from some of the state’s former Republican governors.

item.title: Texas Gov. Greg Abbott (R) loses his bid for a fourth term, falling to Gina Hinojosa (D), according to AP
item.description: Hinojosa, who serves in the state legislature, will be Texas’s first Democratic governor in more than 30 years.

item.title: Sherrod Brown (D) wins Senate race in Ohio, toppling incumbent Jon Husted (R), according to AP
item.description: Ohio was one of Democrats’ prime targets for flipping a GOP Senate seat. Brown previously spent 18 years in the chamber before losing in 2024 as the state turned increasingly Republican.
